topic_title: Present Tense Mastery + SBI PO Level Error Detection

intro_payload.title: Present Tense — Zero to Officer Level
intro_payload.subtitle: SBI PO / BPSC / SSC / Railway Error Detection Special
learning_outcomes: Simple Present, Present Continuous, Present Perfect, Present Perfect Continuous — full mastery
Third person singular -s/-es rules & spelling traps
Stative (non-continuous) verbs — the exception every exam loves
Since/For, Just/Already/Yet, subject-verb agreement special cases
Universal truths, scheduled future, historical present usage
SBI PO / BPSC style sentence error-detection practice with real traps

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir, meri mummy roz subah 6 baje uthti hain aur chai banati hain.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Achha bataya Raju! Notice karo — 'uthti hain', 'banati hain' — ye kaam roz hota hai, ye koi ek din ki baat nahi hai, ye habit hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Haan sir, ye to har din ka niyam hai, hamesha hota hai.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Jab koi kaam REGULARLY ya HAMESHA hota hai, English mein uske liye ek special tense use hota hai. Chalo dekhte hain wo kya hai.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Raju, Hindi grammar mein tumne 'Vartaman Kaal' padha hoga — jo abhi ho raha hai ya jo hamesha sach hai, uske liye.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Haan sir! 'Main khel raha hoon' ya 'Suraj purab se nikalta hai' jaisa?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ekdum sahi examples! English mein isko 'Present Tense' kehte hain. Jab bhi verb 'ta hoon, ti hai, te hain' jaisa Hindi word ho, samjho Present Tense hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achhaaaa! Toh 'main so raha hoon' bhi present hi hoga?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul Raju! Present Tense ke bhi 4 types hote hain — Simple Present, Present Continuous, Present Perfect, aur Present Perfect Continuous. Jaise Past Tense ke bhi 4 the.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Hain?? Char alag types? Sir ye to exam me pakka confuse karega, kaise yaad rakhun sabko!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Tension mat lo, har ek ka apna clear signal word hota hai — jaise 'every day', 'now', 'since/for', 'already'. Pattern samajh gaye to kabhi galti nahi hogi.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Chaliye sir, shuru karte hain sabse pehla wala!

guess_payload.question: Raju, guess karo — inme se kaunsa sentence PRESENT TENSE dikhata hai?
guess_payload.explanation: Sahi jawab C hai! 'Play' base form hai aur 'every day' ek habitual/regular time marker hai — ye Simple Present dikhata hai.

quiz_payload.question: Present Tense ke kitne main types hote hain?
quiz_payload.explanation: Chaar types: Simple Present, Present Continuous, Present Perfect, Present Perfect Continuous — Past Tense ki tarah hi structure hai.

quiz_payload.question: 'Suraj poorab se nikalta hai' — ye sentence kis category mein aata hai?
quiz_payload.explanation: Universal truths (jo hamesha sach hain, jaise Sun rises in the east) Simple Present Tense mein likhe jaate hain, chahe baat kisi bhi time period ki ho rahi ho.

quiz_payload.question: 'Vartaman Kaal' English grammar ke kis concept se match karta hai?
quiz_payload.explanation: 'Vartaman Kaal' ka English mein equivalent 'Present Tense' hai — jo abhi ho raha ho ya hamesha sach ho, uske liye use hota hai.

milestone_payload.title: MODULE COMPLETED!
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: Foundation set hai! Ab Simple Present ki deep dive karte hain — SSC/Railway ka favourite topic.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Simple Present Tense use hota hai regular habits, daily routines aur universal truths ke liye. Structure: Subject + V1 (base form).

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Matlab jaise 'I play cricket' — bina koi extra word ke?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul! Par ek zaroori twist hai — jab subject THIRD PERSON SINGULAR ho (He, She, It, ya koi naam jaise Ram, Cat), tab verb mein '-s' ya '-es' lagta hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Hain?? Ye extra 's' kyun lagana padta hai sir?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ye English grammar ka rule hai Raju — 'He plays', 'She goes', 'It rains'. Lekin 'I play', 'You play', 'We play', 'They play' mein '-s' NAHI lagta.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh sirf He/She/It (ya single naam) ke saath hi 's' lagana hai?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Exactly! Isko yaad rakhne ka tarika hai — jab subject EK vyakti/cheez ho (singular, third person), tab verb ke saath 's/es' aayega.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Ye toh SSC ka pakka common trap hoga — 'He play' jaisa galat sentence dikha ke!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Sahi pakda! Ab spelling rules dekho: 1) Normal verb mein bas '-s' — play→plays. 2) Verb jo s,x,z,ch,sh se khatam ho, uspe '-es' — go→goes, wash→washes, catch→catches.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Aur kuch aur bhi rule hai kya?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Haan! 3) Consonant+y se khatam hone wali verb mein 'y' ko 'i' banake '-es' — study→studies, cry→cries, fly→flies. Lekin vowel+y ho to seedha 's' — play→plays, buy→buys.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Toh 'play' mein 'a' vowel hai isliye 'plays', but 'study' mein 't' consonant hai isliye 'studies'!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ruko, do special irregular verbs bhi yaad rakho: 'Have' third person singular mein 'Has' banti hai — 'He has a car', 'do' banti hai 'does' — 'She does her homework'.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir 'He haves' bolna galat hoga toh?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul galat! 'Haves' jaisa word exist hi nahi karta English mein. Yahi BPSC/SSC ka classic trap hai — 'has' hi sahi hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Note kar liya — have→has, do→does, third person singular ke saath!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Negative/Question banane ke liye 'do/does' aata hai, aur uske baad verb WAPAS V1 (base form) mein chali jaati hai — 's/es' hat jaata hai. 'He does not play' — 'play' hi rahega, 'plays' nahi.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Hain?? Toh 'He does not plays' galat hai?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi trap pakda! Yahi 'Double Agreement Error' kehlata hai — 'does' khud third person singular dikha raha hai, dobara verb pe 's' mat lagao.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Ohh matlab jaise Past Tense mein 'did+V2' galat tha, waise hi yahan 'does+V(s)' galat hai!

quiz_payload.question: Kaunsa sentence vyakaran ki drishti se sahi hai?

options.text: She does not plays the piano.
She does not play the piano.
She do not play the piano.

quiz_payload.explanation: 'Does' ke baad verb hamesha V1 (base form) mein aati hai. 'Does not play' sahi hai, 'does not plays' Double Agreement Error hai.

quiz_payload.question: 'Study' verb ka third person singular (He/She/It) form kya hoga?
quiz_payload.explanation: Consonant + y wale verbs mein y ko i banake -es lagate hain: study → studies. 'Studys' aur 'Studyes' dono galat spelling traps hain.

quiz_payload.question: Error Detection: 'He (A)/ have a beautiful house (B)/ near the river (C)/ No error (D)'
quiz_payload.explanation: 'He' third person singular hai, isliye 'have' ki jagah 'has' aayega. Sahi: 'He has a beautiful house'.

milestone_payload.title: MODULE COMPLETED!
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: Simple Present pakka ho gaya! Ab dekhte hain 'abhi ho raha' kaam kaise likhte hain — Present Continuous!

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir, abhi is waqt main aapse baat kar RAHA HOON — ye kaunsa tense hoga?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bahut badhiya example Raju! 'Kar raha hoon' — matlab kaam ABHI, ISI WAQT ho raha hai. Isko Present Continuous Tense kehte hain.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh ye Simple Present se alag hai kyunki isme kaam 'chal raha' hai, roz ka habit nahi hai?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Exactly! Simple Present = habit/routine, Present Continuous = is exact moment mein chal raha kaam.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Structure: Subject + is/am/are + V-ing. 'I' ke saath 'am', 'He/She/It' ke saath 'is', 'You/We/They' ke saath 'are'.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Matlab 'I am eating' sahi hai, 'I is eating' galat?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Sahi pakda! Ye subject-verb agreement ka basic hai — is/am/are ka galat use SSC-Railway ka bahut common trap hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh mujhe hamesha subject dekh ke is/am/are choose karna hai.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Present Continuous ke 3 uses yaad rakho: 1) Is waqt ho raha kaam — 'She is cooking now.' 2) Temporary situation jo abhi chal rahi ho — 'He is staying with us these days.'

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Aur teesra use, sir?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: 3) Near/Fixed Future plans — 'I am meeting him tomorrow.' Ye ek special exception hai jo aage detail mein dekhenge.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Hain?? Present Continuous se Future bhi bata sakte hain?? Ye toh confusing hai!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ruko, ab exam ka sabse bada trap suno — STATIVE VERBS. Kuch verbs 'state/feeling/possession' dikhati hain, unke saath '-ing' KABHI nahi lagta — jaise: know, believe, love, hate, want, need, have (possession), understand, seem.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Matlab 'I am knowing him' galat hoga?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: ⭐ BILKUL SAHI! 'I am knowing him' ek classic wrong sentence hai jo exam mein baar baar aata hai. Sahi hoga: 'I know him.' Stative verbs Simple Present mein hi rehti hain.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh mujhe ye stative verbs ki list yaad rakhni padegi — know, want, need, love, hate, believe!

quiz_payload.question: Kaunsa sentence sahi hai?

options.text: I am understanding this concept now.
I am understand this concept now.

quiz_payload.explanation: 'Understand' ek stative verb hai (mental state), isliye '-ing' form use nahi hoti. Sahi: 'I understand this concept now'.

quiz_payload.question: Error Detection: 'They (A)/ is playing football (B)/ in the ground right now (C)/ No error (D)'
quiz_payload.explanation: 'They' plural subject hai, isliye 'are' aayega, 'is' nahi. Sahi: 'They are playing football'.

quiz_payload.question: Error Detection: 'I (A)/ am wanting a cup of tea (B)/ right now (C)/ No error (D)'
quiz_payload.explanation: 'Want' ek stative verb hai (desire dikhata hai), isliye continuous form nahi lagti. Sahi: 'I want a cup of tea'.

milestone_payload.title: MODULE COMPLETED!
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: Stative verb ka trap crack kar diya! Ab Present Perfect ki taraf chalte hain.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir, 'Maine apna homework kar liya hai' — ye kaunsa tense hoga? 'kiya' bhi hai aur 'hai' bhi hai, confuse ho gaya!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bahut acha observation Raju! Yahan kaam past mein hua hai LEKIN uska EFFECT ya RESULT abhi PRESENT mein dikh raha hai — homework abhi complete hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Matlab past aur present dono connect ho rahe hain isme?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi pakda! Isi ko Present Perfect Tense kehte hain — jab past ka kaam present se JUDA hua ho.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Structure: Subject + have/has + V3 (past participle). 'I/You/We/They' ke saath 'have', 'He/She/It' ke saath 'has'. 'I have done my homework.'

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh V3 wahi hai jo Past Perfect mein bhi use hoti thi — had+V3?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi yaad rakha! V3 same rehti hai, bas helping verb badalta hai — Past Perfect mein 'had', Present Perfect mein 'have/has'.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Toh 'go' ka V3 'gone' hoga, 'She has gone' sahi, 'She has went' galat!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Present Perfect ke saath 'Since' aur 'For' bahut aate hain. Universal Rule: 'Since' = FIXED POINT (since 2015, since Monday, since morning). 'For' = DURATION (for 3 years, for two hours).

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir 'I have lived here since 5 years' sahi hoga kya?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: ⭐ Nahi! Yahi BPSC/SSC ka classic trap hai — '5 years' duration hai, isliye 'for' aayega — 'I have lived here for 5 years'. 'Since' hota tabhi jab fixed point ho, jaise 'since 2018'.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Since = point (2018 se), For = duration (5 saal se) — yaad rakh liya sir!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ab teen important signal words dekho: 'Just' (abhi abhi kiya) — 'I have just finished.' 'Already' (expect se pehle ho gaya) — 'He has already left.' 'Yet' (abhi tak nahi, sirf negative/questions mein) — 'Have you finished yet?'

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Matlab 'yet' sirf negative ya question mein aata hai, positive mein nahi?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! 'I have finished yet' GALAT hai. Positive statement mein 'already' aata hai, negative mein 'yet' — 'I haven't finished yet.'

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Ye toh bahut fine difference hai, exam mein dhyan se dekhna padega!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Sabse bada trap suno Raju — Present Perfect ke saath DEFINITE past time markers (yesterday, last year, ago, in 2015) KABHI use nahi hote.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Matlab 'I have gone there yesterday' galat hoga?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: ⭐ Ekdum sahi! 'Yesterday' ek specific/definite past time hai — isliye sirf Simple Past chalega: 'I went there yesterday'. Present Perfect mein time specify nahi hota, sirf result matter karta hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh Present Perfect ke saath specific date/time nahi bata sakte, sirf 'already/just/since/for/ever/never' jaise words chalenge!

quiz_payload.question: Sahi sentence chuno:

options.text: She has completed the project two days ago.
She completed the project two days ago.
She has completed the project since two days.
She had completed the project two days ago now.

quiz_payload.explanation: 'Two days ago' ek definite past time marker hai, isliye Present Perfect nahi chalega, sirf Simple Past chalega — 'completed'.

quiz_payload.question: Error Detection: 'He (A)/ has been living in Patna (B)/ since three years (C)/ No error (D)'
quiz_payload.explanation: 'Three years' ek duration hai, isliye 'for' aayega, 'since' nahi. Sahi: 'for three years'.

quiz_payload.question: 'Yet' ka sahi use kaunsa hai?

options.text: I have finished my work yet.
I have not finished my work yet.
I am finishing my work yet.

quiz_payload.explanation: 'Yet' sirf negative statements aur questions mein use hota hai, positive statement mein nahi. Sahi: 'I have not finished my work yet'.

milestone_payload.title: MODULE COMPLETED!
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: Past-Present connection ka raja seekh liya! Ab uski cousin — Present Perfect Continuous dekhte hain.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir agar main 2 ghante se yahan padh RAHA HOON, abhi bhi padh raha hoon, isko kya bolenge?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Badhiya sawal! Yahan 'padhna' ek DURATION tak chal raha hai aur ABHI BHI JAARI hai. Ye Present Perfect Continuous hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Matlab isme 'kitni der se' bhi bataya jaata hai aur kaam abhi bhi chal raha hai?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul! Ye tense use hota hai jab kaam PAST mein shuru hua, ab tak CONTINUE ho raha hai, aur abhi bhi khatam nahi hua.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Structure: Subject + have/has been + V-ing. 'I have been studying for 2 hours.' 'She has been waiting since morning.'

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh 'been' hamesha aayega, bas have/has subject ke hisaab se badlega?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Sahi! 'I/You/We/They' ke saath 'have been', 'He/She/It' ke saath 'has been'. Aur uske baad verb hamesha '-ing' form mein hogi.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Note kar liya — have/has been + V-ing, since/for wale rule wahi rahenge yahan bhi!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Raju, ek zaroori difference samjho — Present Perfect (have/has+V3) COMPLETION dikhata hai, Present Perfect Continuous (have/has been+V-ing) CONTINUATION dikhata hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Matlab dono mein farak sirf 'khatam hua ya abhi chal raha' ka hai?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul! 'I have written 5 pages' (5 pages ka kaam complete ho chuka, ho sakta hai ab likhna band kar diya). 'I have been writing for 2 hours' (2 ghante se likh raha hoon, abhi bhi likh raha hoon).

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achhaaaa! Toh completion=V3, continuation=been+ing — clear ho gaya!

quiz_payload.question: Sahi sentence chuno:

options.text: She have been working here for five years.
She has been working here for five years.
She has being working here for five years.
She is been working here for five years.

quiz_payload.explanation: 'She' third person singular hai isliye 'has been'. Structure hai 'has/have been + V-ing', 'has being' galat structure hai.

quiz_payload.question: Error Detection: 'The workers (A)/ have been digging the road (B)/ since two hours (C)/ No error (D)'
quiz_payload.explanation: 'Two hours' ek duration hai, isliye 'for' aayega, 'since' nahi. Sahi: 'for two hours'.

quiz_payload.question: Present Perfect Continuous kab use hota hai?

options.text: Jab kaam past mein complete ho chuka ho
Jab kaam past mein shuru hua ho aur abhi bhi jaari ho

quiz_payload.explanation: Present Perfect Continuous ek aisa kaam dikhata hai jo past mein shuru hua aur abhi tak jaari hai — 'has/have been + V-ing + since/for'.

milestone_payload.title: MODULE COMPLETED!
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: Chaaron Present Tenses clear ho gaye Raju! Ab dekhte hain kuch special uses jo exam mein pakka aate hain.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ab kuch SPECIAL uses of Simple Present dekhte hain jo BPSC/SSC bahut poochta hai. Pehla: UNIVERSAL TRUTHS/Scientific Facts — 'Water boils at 100°C', 'The Earth revolves around the Sun'.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir isme kaam abhi nahi ho raha, phir bhi Present Tense kyun?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Kyunki ye baatein HAMESHA sach hain — kal bhi sach thi, aaj bhi sach hai, kal bhi sach rahegi. Isiliye chahe baat past mein bhi ho rahi ho, universal truth hamesha Simple Present mein hi likha jaata hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: ⭐ Achha! Toh 'Galileo said that the Earth revolves around the Sun' — 'revolves' hi rahega, 'revolved' nahi?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ekdum sahi Raju! Universal truth reported speech mein bhi change nahi hoti. Ab dusra use dekho: HISTORICAL PRESENT — jab past ki historical events ko interesting/dramatic banane ke liye Present Tense mein likha jaaye.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Matlab jaise story sunane mein bolte hain 'Akbar comes to the throne in 1556'?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi example! Ye zyada tar newspapers headlines, story-telling, aur commentary mein use hota hai — 'Sachin scores a century!' jaise headlines mein.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achhaaaa, matlab news headlines mein bhi Present Tense use hota hai chahe event ho chuka ho!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Teesra use: SCHEDULED/TIMETABLE FUTURE EVENTS. Jab koi kaam FIXED schedule ke hisaab se future mein hoga, tab Simple Present use hota hai — 'The train leaves at 6 PM tomorrow', 'The exam starts next Monday'.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Hain?? Future ki baat, phir bhi Present Tense?? Ye toh confusing hai sir!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Samjho aise — jab kuch FIXED/OFFICIAL timetable ke hisaab se ho (train, flight, school schedule), tab Simple Present. Personal plans ke liye Present Continuous chalta hai — 'I am meeting him tomorrow.'

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh timetable/schedule = Simple Present, personal plan = Present Continuous — dono future ke liye but alag context mein!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: ⭐ Ab sabse bada exam trap suno — Time/Conditional Clauses mein FUTURE TENSE use NAHI hota, chahe overall meaning future ka ho. 'If it rains, we will stay home' — 'if' clause mein Present, main clause mein Future.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir 'If it will rain, we will stay home' galat hoga toh?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: ⭐ BILKUL SAHI PAKDA! Ye SBI PO ka super favourite trap hai. 'If', 'when', 'until', 'as soon as', 'before', 'after' wale clause mein future ki baat bhi Simple Present mein hi likhi jaati hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh main clause mein 'will', but 'if/when' wale clause mein sirf Present — dono milake future meaning banta hai!

quiz_payload.question: Sahi sentence chuno:

options.text: When he will arrive, we will start the meeting.
When he arrives, we will start the meeting.
When he arrived, we will start the meeting.
When he will arrives, we will start the meeting.

quiz_payload.explanation: Time clause ('when') mein future ke liye Simple Present use hota hai, 'will' nahi. Main clause mein 'will start' sahi hai.

quiz_payload.question: Error Detection: 'The teacher told us that (A)/ the sun rose in the east (B)/ and set in the west (C)/ No error (D)'
quiz_payload.explanation: Universal truths tense mein backshift nahi hote, chahe reporting verb Past mein ho. Sahi: 'the sun rises in the east and sets in the west'.

quiz_payload.question: 'The train ___ at 7 AM tomorrow' (fixed railway schedule) — sahi verb form?
quiz_payload.explanation: Fixed timetable/schedule wale future events ke liye Simple Present use hota hai — 'The train leaves at 7 AM tomorrow'.

milestone_payload.title: MODULE COMPLETED!
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: Officer level trap crack kar diya! Ab Subject-Verb Agreement ke deep traps dekhte hain.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ab hum seekhenge Subject-Verb Agreement ke SPECIAL cases jo SBI PO/BPSC mein baar baar aate hain. Universal Rule: Singular Subject → Singular Verb (is/was/has/verb+s), Plural Subject → Plural Verb (are/were/have/verb).

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Ye to easy hai sir, subject dekho aur verb match karo!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Haan lekin kuch SPECIAL subjects hain jinme confusion hoti hai. Pehla: 'Each', 'Every', 'Either', 'Neither' — ye sab hamesha SINGULAR treat hote hain, chahe baad mein plural noun ho.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Matlab 'Each of the boys' singular treat hoga, plural nahi?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi Raju! 'Each of the boys is intelligent' — 'boys' plural hai but 'each' singular banata hai, isliye 'is' aayega. Ab dusra case: COLLECTIVE NOUNS (team, family, jury, class, committee, army).

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir 'team' toh bahut logon ka group hai, isliye 'are' aayega na?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: ⭐ Yahan bada trap hai — Collective nouns NORMALLY singular treat hote hain jab group EK UNIT ki tarah act kar raha ho — 'The team is playing well.' Sirf jab members ALAG-ALAG act kar rahe hon tab plural — 'The team are quarrelling among themselves.'

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achhaaaa! Toh ek saath kaam kare toh singular, alag alag kare toh plural — ye toh bahut fine difference hai!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ab teesra important trap: EITHER...OR / NEITHER...NOR. Rule: Verb hamesha us subject se match karega jo VERB KE SABSE PAAS (closer) ho, na ki pehle wale se.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Matlab 'Either Ram or his friends' — verb 'friends' se match karega kyunki wo paas hai?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! 'Either Ram or his friends ARE responsible' — kyunki 'friends' (plural) verb ke closer hai. Agar order badal dete — 'Either his friends or Ram IS responsible' — kyunki ab 'Ram' (singular) closer hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: ⭐ Ye toh super tricky hai! Hamesha last subject dekhna hai, verb usi se match karna hai!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Aur ek zaroori list — Indefinite pronouns jo HAMESHA singular hote hain: everyone, everybody, everything, someone, somebody, anyone, anybody, no one, nobody, each. Inke saath hamesha singular verb aayega.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh 'Everyone are happy' galat hoga, 'Everyone is happy' sahi?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Ye BPSC ka bahut common trap hai — 'everyone/everybody' bahut logon ki baat karta hai isliye students plural bol dete hain, but grammar mein ye SINGULAR hi treat hota hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Note kar liya sir — every/some/any/no + one/body/thing = singular hamesha!

quiz_payload.question: Sahi sentence chuno:

options.text: Neither of the answers are correct.
Neither of the answers is correct.
Neither of the answers were correct.
Neither of the answers have been correct.

quiz_payload.explanation: 'Neither of' hamesha singular verb leta hai, chahe baad mein plural noun ho. Sahi: 'Neither of the answers is correct'.

quiz_payload.question: Error Detection: 'Either the manager or the employees (A)/ is responsible (B)/ for this mistake (C)/ No error (D)'
quiz_payload.explanation: 'Either...or' mein verb closer subject se match karta hai. Yahan 'employees' (plural) closer hai, isliye 'are' aayega, 'is' galat hai.

quiz_payload.question: Error Detection: 'Everybody in the class (A)/ have submitted (B)/ their assignments on time (C)/ No error (D)'
quiz_payload.explanation: 'Everybody' hamesha singular treat hota hai, isliye 'has submitted' aayega, 'have submitted' galat hai.

milestone_payload.title: MODULE COMPLETED!
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: Ye SBI PO ka toughest module tha aur tumne crack kar liya! Ab kuch aur agreement traps dekhte hain.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ab ek aur important rule — Distance, Money, Time, Weight jab EK SINGLE UNIT/AMOUNT ki tarah treat ho, tab SINGULAR verb aata hai, chahe number plural dikhe.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Matlab 'Two hundred rupees' plural lagta hai, phir bhi singular verb?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul! 'Two hundred rupees is a good amount' — kyunki yahan 'do sau rupaye' ek TOTAL AMOUNT ki tarah treat ho raha hai, individual notes ki tarah nahi. Same rule: 'Ten kilometers is a long distance.'

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: ⭐ Achha! Toh jab total quantity/amount ek group ki tarah socha jaaye, tab singular verb!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ek aur trap: Jab GERUND (V-ing form jo noun ki tarah kaam kare) subject ho, verb hamesha SINGULAR aata hai. 'Playing video games is his favourite hobby.'

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir 'games' plural hai, phir bhi 'is' aaya, kyun?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Kyunki asli subject 'games' nahi, 'Playing' (gerund) hai! Poora gerund phrase 'Playing video games' ek SINGLE ACTIVITY treat hota hai — isliye singular verb.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achhaaaa! Matlab gerund subject ho toh dekho poora phrase ek IDEA hai, uske andar ke words count nahi karte!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Last special case: Jab 'Each' ya 'Every' do subjects ko JOIN karne wale 'and' se PEHLE aaye, tab bhi verb SINGULAR hoga — 'Each boy and each girl HAS received a prize.'

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Hain? 'Boy AND girl' toh do log ho gaye, plural nahi hoga?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: ⭐ Yahi trap hai Raju! Normally 'A and B' plural verb leta hai (Ram and Shyam ARE friends). Lekin agar 'Each'/'Every' pehle laga ho, to power singular kar deta hai — 'Each' ka effect dono subjects pe pड़ता hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh 'Each/Every + noun and noun' = singular, but normal 'noun and noun' = plural. Note kar liya!

quiz_payload.question: Sahi sentence chuno:

options.text: Five kilometers are a long distance to walk.
Five kilometers is a long distance to walk.
Five kilometers were a long distance to walk.
Five kilometers have been a long distance to walk.

quiz_payload.explanation: Distance ek total amount/single unit ki tarah treat hoti hai, isliye singular verb 'is' aayega, plural 'are' nahi.

quiz_payload.question: Error Detection: 'Reading good books (A)/ increase our (B)/ knowledge and vocabulary (C)/ No error (D)'
quiz_payload.explanation: 'Reading good books' ek gerund phrase hai, singular subject treat hota hai. Sahi: 'increases our knowledge'.

quiz_payload.question: Error Detection: 'Each boy and each girl (A)/ in the class have received (B)/ a certificate of merit (C)/ No error (D)'
quiz_payload.explanation: 'Each...and each...' pattern hamesha singular verb leta hai. Sahi: 'has received', 'have received' galat hai.

milestone_payload.title: MODULE COMPLETED!
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: Officer-level agreement mind ban gaya hai tumhara! Ab final module — SBI PO Error Detection Master Practice!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ab hum karenge exact SBI PO style practice — sentence 4 parts mein todke error dhundhna. Strategy: 1) Pehle subject-verb agreement check karo (singular/plural match?). 2) Time markers verb se match kar rahe hain kya?

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Aur kya check karna hai sir?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: 3) Stative verbs pe '-ing' toh nahi laga diya? 4) Since/For sahi jagah use hue hain kya? 5) 'Does/Has' ke baad double 's/es' toh nahi lag gaya verb pe?

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Ye toh ek poori checklist ban gayi sir! Chaliye practice karte hain!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Trap 1: Stative verbs with -ing. Exam mein 'is/am/are + know/want/need/love/hate/believe/seem/own' jaisa combination dikha ke trap bichhaya jaata hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir 'I am owning a car' bhi galat hoga toh?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! 'Own' possession dikhata hai, stative verb hai. Sahi: 'I own a car'. Yaad rakho list: know, believe, love, hate, want, need, have(possession), understand, seem, own, belong, prefer.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir main roz ye list revise karunga, exam tak sab clear ho jaayega!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Trap 2: Double Agreement Error — jab ek hi sentence mein do jagah third-person-s dikha diya jaaye. 'He does not plays' (galat), 'She doesn't goes' (galat).

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh sahi kya hoga in dono ka sir?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: 'He does not play', 'She doesn't go'. Rule: 'Does/Doesn't' khud hi third-person-singular dikha deta hai, isliye verb apni ORIGINAL V1 form mein rahegi.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achhaaaa! 'Does' ke baad kabhi bhi 's/es' wali verb nahi aayegi!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Trap 3: Present Perfect with Definite Time. 'I have met him last week' GALAT hai — 'last week' definite past hai, isliye sirf Simple Past chalega: 'I met him last week'.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh Present Perfect ke saath 'yesterday, last week, ago, in 2020' kabhi nahi aa sakte?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Present Perfect ke saath 'already, just, yet, since, for, ever, never, recently, so far, up till now' jaise words hi aate hain — definite markers se kabhi mix mat karna.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Ye toh SBI PO ka sabse repeat hone wala trap lagta hai sir!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Trap 4: Future in Time/Conditional Clause. 'If he will come, I will meet him' GALAT hai. Sahi: 'If he comes, I will meet him' — 'if/when/until/before/after' clause mein Present, main clause mein Future/will.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir ye same rule 'as soon as' aur 'till' ke saath bhi lagega kya?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Haan bilkul! Sabhi TIME clauses (when, while, before, after, till, until, as soon as) aur CONDITIONAL clauses (if, unless) mein future ki baat ho toh bhi Simple Present hi use hoga.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: ⭐ Note kar liya sir — clause mein 'will' dekha toh turant samajh jaunga ye error hai!

quiz_payload.question: Error Detection: 'The manager (A)/ has submitted the report (B)/ yesterday evening (C)/ No error (D)'
quiz_payload.explanation: 'Yesterday evening' ek definite past time marker hai, isliye Present Perfect (has submitted) nahi chalega. Sahi: 'submitted the report'.

quiz_payload.question: Error Detection: 'If it will rain tomorrow (A)/ we will not be able to (B)/ go for the picnic (C)/ No error (D)'
quiz_payload.explanation: 'If' clause mein future ke liye Simple Present aata hai, 'will' nahi. Sahi: 'If it rains tomorrow'.

quiz_payload.question: Error Detection: 'She (A)/ don't like (B)/ spicy food at all (C)/ No error (D)'
quiz_payload.explanation: 'She' third person singular hai, isliye 'doesn't' aayega, 'don't' nahi. Sahi: 'doesn't like'.

milestone_payload.completed_topic: SBI PO Level Error Detection Practice
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: Tumne poora Present Tense chapter Officer-level pe master kar liya! Ab final revision aur master quiz ka time hai!

revision_points.point: Statement I: Third person singular (He/She/It) verb ke saath -s/-es lagta hai. Statement II: 'Does/Doesn't' ke baad verb V1 (base) form mein aati hai, dobara -s nahi lagta. Dono statements sahi hain — Double Agreement Error exam ka top trap hai.

Statement I: 'is/am/are+V-ing' abhi ho raha kaam dikhata hai. Statement II: Stative verbs (know, want, love, believe, have-possession) ke saath '-ing' kabhi nahi lagta. Dono sahi — 'I am knowing' jaisa sentence hamesha galat hai.

Statement I: 'have/has+V3' past kaam ka present se connection dikhata hai. Statement II: Present Perfect ke saath definite time markers (yesterday, ago, last year) kabhi use nahi hote. Statement I sahi, Statement II bhi sahi — ye BPSC/SSC ka top repeated trap hai.

Statement I: 'If/when/until/before/after' clause mein future ki baat bhi Simple Present mein likhi jaati hai. Statement II: Main clause mein 'will' use hota hai. Dono statements sahi hain — clause mein 'will' dekhna hamesha error hai.

Statement I: 'Each/Every/Either/Neither/Everyone/Everybody' hamesha singular verb lete hain. Statement II: 'Either...or/Neither...nor' mein verb closer subject se match karta hai. Dono statements sahi hain — inko mix karna common error hai.

quiz_payload.question: Assertion-Reason: Assertion (A): 'Each boy and each girl has received a certificate' is grammatically correct. Reason (R): When 'each' or 'every' precedes two subjects joined by 'and', the verb is always singular.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

quiz_payload.explanation: 'Each' before two subjects joined by 'and' makes the subject singular in meaning, hence 'has received' (singular verb) is correct. R correctly explains why A is true.

quiz_payload.question: Multi-Statement: Read the sentence and find which parts contain an error: 'If she will complete the project on time (A) / she is knowing that (B) / she will get a good appraisal this year (C) / No error (D)'. Choose the part(s) with error.
quiz_payload.explanation: Part A error: 'If' clause requires Simple Present, not 'will' — should be 'If she completes'. Part B error: 'Know' is a stative verb, cannot take continuous form — should be 'she knows that'. Part C is correct as it's the main clause with future 'will get'.

quiz_payload.question: BPSC Style: Consider the following statements about Present Tense usage: (1) 'She has been living here since five years' is grammatically correct. (2) 'Neither of the answers are correct' is grammatically correct. (3) 'Ten kilometers is a long distance' correctly uses singular verb for a total quantity. Which of the statements is/are CORRECT?
quiz_payload.explanation: Statement 1 is WRONG — 'five years' is a duration, so 'for' should be used, not 'since'. Statement 2 is WRONG — 'Neither of' takes singular verb 'is', not 'are'. Statement 3 is CORRECT — distance as a total quantity takes singular verb. So only Statement 3 is correct.

quiz_payload.question: Error Detection (SBI PO Level): Find the part with error: 'Playing chess and reading novels (A) / are his favourite hobbies (B) / which he does every evening after office (C) / No error (D)'
quiz_payload.explanation: This sentence is correct as written. Here TWO separate gerund phrases ('Playing chess' AND 'reading novels') are joined by 'and', making a compound plural subject, hence 'are' (plural) is correct. Note: this is different from a SINGLE gerund phrase like 'Playing chess is his hobby' which would take singular verb.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir ek aakhri doubt hai — jab hum kisi ki baat REPORT karte hain, Present Tense kya-kya change hota hai?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Achha poocha! Agar reporting verb Present mein ho (says, tells), tab tense CHANGE NAHI hota — 'He says, "I am happy"' → 'He says that he is happy.'

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Aur agar reporting verb Past mein ho, tab kya hoga?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Tab Backshift hota hai: Simple Present→Simple Past, Present Continuous→Past Continuous, Present Perfect→Past Perfect. Bas universal truths kabhi change nahi hote, wo hamesha Present hi rehte hain — ye tumne pehle hi seekh liya tha!

quiz_payload.question: 'The scientist said, "Water boils at 100 degree Celsius."' Iska sahi Reported Speech kya hoga?

options.text: The scientist said that water boiled at 100 degree Celsius.
The scientist said that water boils at 100 degree Celsius.
The scientist said that water had boiled at 100 degree Celsius.
The scientist told that water boils at 100 degree Celsius.

quiz_payload.explanation: Ye ek universal/scientific truth hai, isliye reporting verb Past mein hone ke baawajood tense BACKSHIFT nahi hoga. 'Water boils' hi rahega — universal truths hamesha Simple Present mein hi likhe jaate hain, chahe reporting kisi bhi tense mein ho.
